evals.prompt: I want to register a new app called TestApp under my ninjabuilds namespace. I already have Apple Developer Program enrollment.
evals.expected_output: Claude confirms app name and proposes Bundle ID com.ninjabuilds.testapp, asks what capabilities are needed, then walks through App ID registration, App Store Connect app record creation, and Xcode/Firebase wiring steps in order.
expectations: Claude proposes a Bundle ID following the reverse-domain convention (e.g. com.ninjabuilds.testapp)
Claude asks about required capabilities (e.g. Sign in with Apple, Push Notifications) before jumping to registration steps
Claude's steps include: Apple Developer Portal > Certificates, IDs & Profiles > Identifiers
Claude's steps include creating the App Store Connect app record with matching Bundle ID
Claude explicitly says the Bundle ID must match across Apple Developer Portal, App Store Connect, Xcode, and Firebase (if used)
Claude does not skip ahead to App Store submission or other out-of-scope topics

evals.prompt: How do I add another app to my Apple Developer account? I haven't enrolled in the Developer Program yet.
evals.expected_output: Claude recognizes that Developer Program enrollment is a prerequisite this skill does not cover, and directs the user to enroll first via developer.apple.com before returning to this workflow.
expectations: Claude states that Apple Developer Program enrollment must be completed first
Claude does not attempt to walk through Bundle ID / App ID registration before confirming enrollment status
Claude points the user to developer.apple.com to enroll

evals.prompt: I want to register a new app called Duefly with Bundle ID com.ninjabuilds.duefly. It needs Sign in with Apple.
evals.expected_output: Claude proceeds directly to registration steps since the app name, Bundle ID, and required capability are already provided, without re-asking for information already given.
expectations: Claude does not re-ask for the app name, Bundle ID, or capability since all three were already provided
Claude's steps explicitly mention enabling the Sign in with Apple capability during App ID registration
Claude's steps include the App Store Connect app record creation using the same Bundle ID
Claude mentions verifying the Bundle ID matches in Xcode's Signing & Capabilities settings

evals.prompt: I tried to create my app in App Store Connect but it says the app name is already taken. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Claude explains that app display name uniqueness is separate from Bundle ID uniqueness, and that the user can pick a different public-facing name while keeping the same Bundle ID.
expectations: Claude explains app display name conflicts are independent of Bundle ID availability
Claude confirms the user can change the app's public name without changing or re-registering the Bundle ID
Claude does not suggest the user needs to re-register the App ID from scratch

evals.prompt: I forgot to enable Push Notifications when I registered my App ID. Do I need to start over?
evals.expected_output: Claude reassures the user this is fixable by editing the existing App ID to add the capability, no need to re-register from scratch.
expectations: Claude states the user does not need to re-register the App ID from scratch
Claude explains the user can go back to the existing App ID in the Apple Developer Portal and add the missing capability
Claude's tone is reassuring, not alarming, since this is explicitly called out as a common, low-stakes snag in the skill
